title: Spanakopita
subtitle: Greek spinach and feta pie in crisp filo pastry
excerpt: Layers of buttered filo filled with a savoury mixture of wilted spinach, crumbled feta, egg and herbs. The result is shattering crisp on the outside and creamy and savoury within.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Greek spanakopita preparations.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked: assemble fully, wrap tightly in cling film and freeze for up to 2 months. Bake from frozen, adding 15 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The spinach and feta filling can be made up to a day ahead and refrigerated. Assemble with the filo just before baking.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 170 C. The pie needs sustained heat to crisp every layer of filo.

content.text: You will need one packet of ready-made filo pastry (about 270 g, which gives roughly 12 sheets). Buy it from a supermarket chilled aisle or a Greek or Middle Eastern deli. Filo dries out and cracks within minutes of exposure to air, so keep the stack covered with a damp tea towel as you work. The filling must be completely cool and squeezed very dry before it goes anywhere near the pastry, or the bottom layers will turn soggy.

items.prepNote: fresh baby spinach, or 400 g frozen spinach fully defrosted and squeezed dry
for frying the onion and brushing the filo with butter

content.text: Wilt the spinach. If using fresh spinach, pack it into a large saucepan with just the water clinging to the leaves after washing. Cover and cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring once, until wilted. Tip into a colander and leave to cool. Once cool enough to handle, gather the spinach into a ball and squeeze out as much liquid as you possibly can. Squeeze again. The filling must be dry.

Cook the onion. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced red onion and cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Remove from the heat and leave to cool completely.

Make the filling. Roughly chop the squeezed spinach. Combine in a bowl with the cooled onion, crumbled feta, beaten eggs, spring onion, parsley and nutmeg. Season with black pepper only; the feta provides plenty of salt. Mix well. Taste and adjust if needed.
Preheat the oven to 190 C (fan 170 C). Lightly brush a baking tray or roasting tin roughly 30 cm x 20 cm with the butter and oil mixture.

Layer the base. Lay one sheet of filo in the tray, allowing it to overhang the edges. Brush all over with the butter and oil mix. Repeat with 5 more sheets, brushing each one. Keep the remaining sheets covered with a damp tea towel.
Add the filling. Spread the spinach and feta mixture evenly over the base layers of filo, pressing it down gently. It should form a layer about 3 cm thick.

Top with more filo. Lay the remaining filo sheets over the filling one at a time, brushing each with butter and oil as before. Fold the overhanging base layers up and over the top to seal the edges. Brush the top generously with the remaining butter mix. Score the top lightly with a knife into portions: this makes it much easier to cut after baking.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is deep golden and shattering crisp. Leave to rest for 10 minutes before cutting through the scored lines and serving.

items.cause: The spinach filling was too wet when spread over the pastry.
items.fix: Squeeze the spinach harder next time; the rule is squeeze, then squeeze again. If baked and already soggy, slide the pie onto a wire rack and return to the oven at a low heat to dry out the base.

items.symptom: Filo cracks and tears as you layer it
items.cause: The filo dried out after being exposed to air for too long.
items.fix: Keep the unused sheets covered with a damp (not wet) tea towel at all times. Work as quickly as possible. Cracked sheets can still be used; just overlap the pieces and they will stick together with the butter.

items.symptom: Pie is pale and not crisp after the stated time
items.cause: Oven temperature was too low, or the butter layers were not generous enough.
items.fix: Increase the oven temperature by 10 C and give it another 10 minutes. Brush any pale spots with extra melted butter and return to the oven.

items.cause: The egg ratio was off, or the feta used was mild.
items.fix: Add more feta and season with black pepper. A small grating of fresh nutmeg also lifts the flavour considerably.
